Kanban: Added new tool that gives you Kanban boards for tracking work, with cards you drag between columns.
Attach files to a card or to any individual comment. Images, video and audio play in the card; anything else opens in whatever program owns it. Ctrl+V pastes an image straight from the clipboard.
Priority and Effort are both five levels plus None, and you can rename every level and set its color in the tool's Setup, with a reset back to the defaults.
Tags live in categories, so you can have a Types category holding Bug and Feature, and a Versions category holding your releases, and filter on each independently.
A card's color can come from the card itself, from its tags, or from its priority, set per board and overridable on any single card.
Rearrange the blocks inside a card with the Card Layout editor, as a default and again per board if one board wants a different shape.
Nearly every board preference can be set once for the tool and then overridden on individual boards.

Kanban Setup has a Defaults tab for what every board follows unless it says otherwise, and Board Setup's Overrides tab lists a board's own answers grouped the same way. Overdue warnings can be switched off per board.

Select several cards at once with Ctrl+click or Shift+click, then set their priority, effort, tags, owner or column in one go from the right-click menu, or drag them all together. The board's card count tells you how many are selected, and the selection stays put after an action so a second change to the same cards is one more right-click.
Sort any column by priority, effort, due date and more without losing the order you dragged it into, as a board default or per column.
Sort the board gallery by newest, oldest, name, most recently opened or most used, or just drag the boards into your own order.
Search a board's tags right from the card, create a new one on the spot when it doesn't exist yet, and drag tags and tag categories into whatever order you want.
Archive cards one at a time, in bulk, or a whole column at once, and restore them whenever.
Reset a board's card numbering, so deleting a pile of test cards doesn't leave your first real card stuck as #4. It never hands out a number a card still has.
A card carrying a description shows a notepad on its face, so you can tell there is more inside it without opening it.
Stage dates track when a card started, went to testing, and finished. An Advance button stamps the next one with the current date/time, and every date (except created) stays directly editable.

A column can stamp a stage date by itself. Set it to Work Started or Testing Started in Column Settings, or mark the column as meaning done to stamp Completed, and a card moved in gets that date and the time it happened, if it doesn't have one already.
Boards, cards and their attachments are included in the app's snapshots and in the Data tab's export and import.
You can connect a local AI coding agent to a single board so it can read and change cards while you work in it, using Claude Code, OpenAI's Codex, or anything else that speaks MCP.

The agent talks to the app over a local pipe, so that connection never leaves your computer, and the app itself decides every request rather than trusting the agent to check. Most agents run on their provider's servers though, so whatever the agent reads from your board goes to that provider.
Board Setup > Agents is where you switch it on, and every permission starts off. Grant only creating cards, or add editing, moving, tagging, etc. as you need them.

Connecting an agent is one paste: pick your agent, press Copy Command, and paste it into Command Prompt or PowerShell. It sets the agent up, replaces any older connection for that board, and reports whether it worked. Editors like Cursor and VS Code get a config block for their settings file instead.
Each connection shows when an agent last used it, and the board shows when an agent is active on it right now.
Every request an agent makes, passed or refused, is logged in Board Setup > Agents, and a refused one says which switch would have allowed it.

App Overall: Added ability to opt-in to New Version Notifications from General Settings.
This is the first and only time this app ever makes a network call; it pings GitHub to see the latest released version.
This happens once on app launch, and also once when you enable this setting (so you don't have to relaunch to check).
If the version you're on is older than the latest released version, the top bar of the Home Page will indicate an update is available and link to the About modal.
The button to launch the About modal will also pulsate to indicate that a newer version is available.
You can quickly get to the GitHub Releases Page from this notification in the About modal.
From the About Modal, you can also select to Ignore This Version if you want to skip updating this version, but still get future update available notifications.

This feature is opt-in, off by default, and can be disabled at any time after enabling. No data ever leaves your device; this is a read-only check on GitHub for the sole purpose of checking the latest available Release.

Auto-Backup: Added new tool that allows you to define one or many source folders and one or multiple destination folders for a backup.
Browse for folders via Windows, or add raw paths manually. You can also double-click a path to inline edit it.
Uses Windows' robocopy utility to mirror the entirety of the source folder(s) (and any subfolders / files) to each of the Destination folders.
Only new / modified files get mirrored over to save time. If the Destination folder already has the same file, it will be skipped.
Note that the point of this tool is to exactly 'mirror' the Source folder structure / contents into the Destination.
For future backups, this means that files changed in the Source will overwrite older versions in the Destination.
This also means that files that are no longer in the Source will be removed from the Destination.
You can create Presets of commonly used Source / Destination Folder setups.
Stats show in the Summary section, including an 'overestimate' of time to complete the backup.
Backup progress is then shown in the Last Run section at the bottom. A summary log .txt file is included in the first Destination folder provided.
